blocks.label: Pre-mid vs post-mid
blocks.text: Pre-mid = everything up to **information gain in decision trees**. Everything after that, including decision-tree overfitting, kNN and LWR, is post-mid. Across all four papers (160 marks) the split is **15% / 85%**.

blocks.label: How to use this paper
blocks.text: Open **Worked problems** and try each question on paper before revealing the steps.

worked.title: Q1 · kNN with three values of k (5 marks)

problem.text: Training points: X1 (−1,1) −, X2 (0,1) +, X3 (0,2) −, X4 (1,−1) −, X5 (1,0) +, X6 (1,2) +, X7 (2,2) −, X8 (2,3) +. Classify (1,1) with k = 7, then k = 3 and k = 5. What is the final class over all three?

steps.label: k = 3
steps.text: X2, X5, X6 → 3 + ⇒ **Positive**

steps.label: k = 5
steps.text: Add X3, X7 → 3 +, 2 − ⇒ **Positive**

steps.label: k = 7
steps.text: Add X1, X4 → 3 +, 4 − ⇒ **Negative**

steps.label: Final
steps.text: Two of the three k values say + ⇒ **Positive**.

problem.text: Positive: x = 7, 9, 11. Negative: x = 0, 8, 10, 12 (on the x-axis). Find a separating hyperplane using the kernel trick and plot before and after.

steps.label: Before
steps.text: In order: 0 −, 7 +, 8 −, 9 +, 10 −, 11 +, 12 −. The labels alternate, so the data is **not linearly separable** on the line.

steps.label: Transform
steps.text: φ(x) = x mod 2: positives (odd) → 1, negatives (even) → 0.

steps.label: Hyperplane
steps.text: **y = 0.5** separates the two levels with maximum margin.

worked.title: Q3 · Regression through the origin (7 marks)

problem.text: Data (x, y): (1,3), (1,2), (2,1), (3,3), (5,3), (7,7), (6,4), (7,6), (6,7), (4,5). Model y = wx. (A) Compute E(w) = Σ(y − wx)² for w = −1, −0.4, −0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 1 and mark the global minimum. (B) Give the best hypothesis and predict y at x = 7.6.

steps.label: Expand
steps.text: E(w) = Σy² − 2wΣxy + w²Σx²

steps.label: (B)
steps.text: Best hypothesis h(x) = 0.920x. At x = 7.6: **ŷ ≈ 6.99 ≈ 7**.

worked.title: Q4 · Information gain with a corrupted bit (7 marks)

problem.text: A, B ∈ {0,1}, label Y. Rows: (1,0,no), (1,1,no), (0,*,no), (0,1,yes), (0,1,yes), (1,1,yes). On the clean data, B was chosen at the root over A by information gain. Can you tell what * was?

steps.label: Conclusion
steps.text: Either way Gain(B) > Gain(A), so B would be at the root whatever * is. The information is **not enough** to recover *.

worked.answer: Gain(A) = 0.082 < Gain(B) (0.191 or 0.459): * cannot be determined.

worked.title: Q5 · MLE for a 4-sided die (3 marks)

problem.text: P(0) = a, P(1) = (1−a)/3, P(2) = (1−a)/2, P(3) = (1−a)/6. Observed rolls: 0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 1, 0. Find the most probable a.

steps.label: Likelihood
steps.text: Two 0s give a²; the six other rolls each give a constant × (1−a). L(a) ∝ **a²(1−a)⁶**.

steps.label: Log and differentiate
steps.text: log L = 2 log a + 6 log(1−a) + const ⇒ 2/a − 6/(1−a) = 0

worked.title: Q6 · Linear SVM: what-ifs (5 marks)

problem.text: Positive: (3,2), (4,3), (2,3), (3,−1). Negative: (1,0), (−1,−1), (0,2), (−1,2). (A) Find the support vectors. (B) Does the hyperplane change if (a) (2,3) is removed, (b) (−2,−3) is added?

steps.label: (A)
steps.text: Support vectors: **(2,3), (3,−1)** and **(1,0)**. They give w = (8/7, 2/7), b = −15/7, i.e. 8x₁ + 2x₂ − 15 = 0. (Same data as Q6 of the 2021 regular paper, where the full working is shown.)

steps.label: (B)(a)
steps.text: (2,3) is a support vector, so the hyperplane **changes**. New SVs (3,2), (3,−1), (1,0) give w = (1,0), b = −2: the new boundary is **x₁ = 2**.

steps.label: (B)(b)
steps.text: f(−2,−3) = (−16 − 6 − 15)/7 = −37/7 < −1: correct side and outside the margin, so it is not a support vector and the hyperplane **does not change**.

worked.answer: SVs (2,3), (3,−1), (1,0); without (2,3) the boundary becomes x₁ = 2; adding (−2,−3) changes nothing.

worked.title: Q7 · AdaBoost with stumps (3 marks)

problem.text: Picture: two − at the top left, three + in the lower middle, two − on the right. Train AdaBoost with stumps until zero training error, circling the points whose weights increase.

steps.label: Round 1
steps.text: Vertical stump: left of the right-hand − points ⇒ +, right ⇒ −. Misclassified: the **two top −** (circle them).

steps.label: Round 2
steps.text: Horizontal stump: above the + points ⇒ −, below ⇒ +. Misclassified: the **two right −** (circle them).

steps.label: After round 2
steps.text: The + points are exactly where both stumps say +, so together the two stumps carve out the + region: **2 iterations**.

steps.label: Strict α-weighted vote
steps.text: If the final classifier is the α-weighted sum of the stumps, two stumps with different α cannot give zero error here: the larger α wins on one of the − groups. A third stump (e.g. y below the upper + level ⇒ +, else −, which misclassifies only the two upper + points) then gives zero training error.

worked.answer: 2 iterations (the two stumps carve out the + region); 3 with a strict α-weighted vote.

worked.title: Q8 · K-means with an outlier (5 marks)

problem.text: Points (−R,0), (−R+1,0), …, (0,0), …, (R,0) and an outlier (10R,0). Two clusters; one centre starts at (0,0). Where should the other start so that one cluster gets every point and the other none? Where do the centres end up?

steps.label: Condition
steps.text: Every point must be closer to (0,0) than to (X,0). For the outlier: |X − 10R| > 10R ⇒ X > 20R or X < 0. For (−R,0): |X + R| > R ⇒ X > 0 or X < −2R. Together: **X > 20R or X < −2R**.

steps.label: Iteration 1
steps.text: All 2R + 2 points go to the first centre. The second centre gets nothing and stays at (X,0).

steps.label: New first centre
steps.text: Mean = (0 + 10R)/(2R + 2) = **(5R/(R+1), 0)**. The points from −R to R sum to 0, so only the outlier moves it.

steps.label: Final
steps.text: Centres **(5R/(R+1), 0)** and **(X, 0)**. For X > 20R nothing changes again. For X just below −2R, check that (−R,0) is still closer to the new first centre: this needs X < −(2R + 5R/(R+1)).

worked.answer: X > 20R or X < −2R; final centres (5R/(R+1), 0) and (X, 0).
